title: CCZ representatives with linear-equivalence automorphisms
summary: Determine whether every quadratic vectorial Boolean function with a nontrivial graph automorphism has a CCZ representative with a nontrivial linear-equivalence automorphism.

formal_statement.body: Let $F:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb F_2^n$ be quadratic and suppose its full graph automorphism group $\operatorname{Aut}(F)$ is nontrivial. Must the CCZ class of $F$ contain a representative $G$ with a nontrivial linear-equivalence automorphism, that is, $$|\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathrm{LE}}(G)|>1?$$ Prove this for every such $F$, or give a counterexample.

scope.domain: Quadratic vectorial Boolean functions and automorphisms of their CCZ classes
assumptions: Automorphism groups use the source definitions
parameters: representative $G$ in the CCZ class of $F$
scope.unresolved_remainder: Prove that the required representative exists for every quadratic F with a nontrivial full automorphism, or exhibit a counterexample CCZ class.

progress.summary: The source asks whether nontrivial full automorphisms of quadratic functions can always be represented by nontrivial linear-equivalence automorphisms inside the CCZ class.
